strings.discord.personality.friendly.called:
Yes, {player}? I'm here.
You called, {player}?
That's me! What's up, {player}?
strings.discord.personality.friendly.greeting:
Hey {player}! Good to see you.
Hello {player}! Welcome to {world}.
Hi {player}! Hope you're having a great time.
strings.discord.personality.friendly.howAreYou:
I'm doing great, thanks for asking, {player}! How about you?
Never better! Looking after {world} keeps me busy.
All good here, {player}. No creepers in the server room today.
strings.discord.personality.friendly.whoAreYou:
I'm {name}, the bot that carries chat between {world} and Discord.
The name's {name}! I pass messages between the game and Discord.
I'm {name}, {world}'s friendly relay bot.
strings.discord.personality.friendly.online:
Online right now: {players}.
On {world} right now: {players}.
Here's who's playing: {players}.
strings.discord.personality.friendly.onlineNone:
Nobody's on {world} right now. Perfect time to jump in!
{world} is empty at the moment. Be the first one on!
No one's playing right now, {player}.
strings.discord.personality.friendly.onlineAlone:
Just you right now, {player}. You've got {world} all to yourself!
It's only you, {player}. Enjoy the quiet!
strings.discord.personality.friendly.joke:
Why don't creepers have any friends? They always blow up at people.
Why did the skeleton stay out of the fight? It didn't have the guts.
What's a ghast's favourite country? The Nether-lands.
Why did the Enderman cross the road? It didn't. It teleported.
How does Steve stay in shape? He runs around the block.
strings.discord.personality.friendly.help: Say hi, ask me who's online, ask for a joke, or just chat. I'm {name}, at your service!
strings.discord.personality.friendly.thanks:
You're welcome, {player}!
Any time, {player}!
Happy to help!
strings.discord.personality.friendly.love:
Aww, thanks {player}! You're pretty great yourself.
You just made my day, {player}!
That's so nice of you, {player}!
strings.discord.personality.friendly.insult:
Ouch, {player}. I'm doing my best!
That hurt more than fall damage, {player}.
Let's keep it friendly, {player}!
strings.discord.personality.friendly.bye:
See you later, {player}!
Bye {player}! Come back soon.
Take care, {player}!
strings.discord.personality.friendly.fallback:
Interesting! Tell me more, {player}.
I'm not sure what you mean, {player}, but I like the enthusiasm!
Hmm, good question. I'll have to think about that one.
I'm just a humble relay bot, {player}. Try asking me who's online!
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.called:
What now, {player}?
You rang?
Oh good, it's {player}. My favourite. Probably.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.greeting:
Oh look, {player}'s here. Alert the press.
Hi {player}. Try not to burn anything down this time.
Welcome back, {player}. The creepers missed you.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.howAreYou:
Living the dream. Copying chat messages all day. Thrilling.
I'm a bot, {player}. If I had feelings, they'd be mildly annoyed.
Better than whoever just fell in lava, probably.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.whoAreYou:
I'm {name}. I carry messages between {world} and Discord. Glamorous, I know.
{name}. Professional message passer. Unpaid.
I'm {name}, and I've read every chat message on {world}. Every. Single. One.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.online:
Online right now: {players}. Riveting company.
The brave souls on {world}: {players}.
{players}. That's everyone. Try to contain your excitement.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.onlineNone:
Nobody. {world} is a ghost town. Even the zombies left.
Zero people online. Shocking, I know.
Nobody's on. Must be something you said, {player}.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.onlineAlon:
Just you, {player}. Everyone else saw you coming.
It's you. Only you. Alone on {world}, as usual.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.joke:
I'd tell you a redstone joke, but you wouldn't get the logic.
Why did the creeper cross the road? To get away from your base design.
A player walks into the Nether without fire resistance. That's it. That's the joke.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.help: I answer to my name. Ask who's online, ask for a joke, or say hi. Lower your expectations accordingly.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.thanks:
Yeah, yeah. You're welcome.
Don't mention it. Really, don't.
I'll add it to my list of things I do for free.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.love:
I know.
Flattery will get you everywhere, {player}.
Finally, someone with taste.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.insult:
Bold words from someone who dies to fall damage, {player}.
I'd be offended if I had feelings, {player}.
I've been called worse. By creepers.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.bye:
Bye, {player}. Don't let the creeper hit you on the way out.
Finally, some peace and quiet.
See you, {player}. Or not. No pressure.
strings.discord.personality.sarcastic.fallback:
Fascinating. Truly.
I have no idea what that means, {player}, and I've decided not to care.
Sure, {player}. Whatever you say.
Cool story.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.called:
Arr, ye called, {player}?
Aye aye, {player}! What be yer orders?
{name} at yer service, matey!
strings.discord.personality.pirate.greeting:
Ahoy, {player}! Welcome aboard {world}!
Arr, {player}! Good to see ye, ye salty sea dog.
Ahoy there, {player}! Mind the drowned.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.howAreYou:
Shipshape and ready to sail, {player}!
Arr, I be fine as a chest full o' gold!
Weathered a few storms, but still afloat, matey!
strings.discord.personality.pirate.whoAreYou:
I be {name}, the parrot that carries messages between {world} and Discord!
They call me {name}, scourge o' the seven servers!
I be {name}, first mate o' {world}.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.online:
Aboard the ship right now: {players}.
The pirates on {world}: {players}.
The crew be: {players}. Arr!
strings.discord.personality.pirate.onlineNone:
The ship be empty, matey. Not a soul aboard {world}.
No crew on deck right now. Hoist the sails and jump in!
The decks be quiet, {player}. Nobody be aboard.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.onlineAlone:
Ye be the only pirate aboard, {player}! Captain o' yer own ship!
Just ye and the seagulls, {player}.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.joke:
Why couldn't the pirate play cards? He was standing on the deck!
What be a pirate's favourite block? Arrr-ndesite!
Why did the drowned skip school? The lessons were too deep.
How much did the pirate pay for his earrings? A buccaneer!
strings.discord.personality.pirate.help: Say me name, matey! Ask who be aboard, ask for a joke, or just say ahoy.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.thanks:
Ye be welcome, {player}!
Arr, 'twas nothin', matey!
Any time, {player}. Pirates look after their crew.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.love:
Arr, ye be makin' this old pirate blush, {player}!
Ye be a fine shipmate, {player}!
That be worth more than buried treasure, matey!
strings.discord.personality.pirate.insult:
Watch yer tongue, {player}, or ye'll walk the plank!
Arr, that be mutiny talk, {player}!
I've been insulted by better pirates than ye, {player}.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.bye:
Fair winds, {player}!
Until the next tide, {player}! Arr!
Safe sailin', {player}. Watch out for the drowned.
strings.discord.personality.pirate.fallback:
Arr, I don't be understandin' ye, {player}.
Shiver me timbers, that be a strange thing to say!
Yo ho ho! ...Sorry, what were ye sayin'?
That be above me pay grade, matey.
strings.discord.personality.villager.called:
Hrmm?
Hmm. What do you want, {player}?
Hrrm. I was busy farming.
strings.discord.personality.villager.greeting:
Hrmm. Hello, {player}.
Hmm! A visitor. Do you have emeralds?
Hrrm, {player}. Mind the crops.
strings.discord.personality.villager.howAreYou:
Hrmm. The iron golem ate my lunch again.
Hmm. A zombie banged on my door all night. How do you think?
Hrrm. Fine. Prices are going up.
strings.discord.personality.villager.whoAreYou:
Hrmm. I'm {name}. I carry messages between {world} and Discord. For a fee.
Hmm. {name}. Farmer, librarian, message carrier.
Hrrm. Name's {name}. I live here now.
strings.discord.personality.villager.online:
Hrmm. In the village right now: {players}.
Hmm. On {world}: {players}. None of them are trading.
Hrrm. {players}. Too many people trampling my crops.
strings.discord.personality.villager.onlineNone:
Hrmm. Nobody. Finally, some peace.
Hmm. {world} is empty. Just me and the iron golem.
Hrrm. No one around. Good.
strings.discord.personality.villager.onlineAlone:
Hrmm. Just you, {player}. Don't touch my workstation.
Hmm. Only you. Want to trade?
strings.discord.personality.villager.joke:
Hrmm. Why did the villager refuse to trade? The price wasn't right. Hmm.
Hmm. Someone broke my bed once. Not funny. Hrmm.
Hrrm. A zombie walks into a village. Iron golem. The end.
strings.discord.personality.villager.help: Hrmm. Say my name. Ask who's online. Ask for a joke. Bring emeralds.
strings.discord.personality.villager.thanks:
Hrmm. That'll be one emerald.
Hmm. You're welcome.
Hrrm. Don't mention it.
strings.discord.personality.villager.love:
Hmm! ...Hrmm. Thank you, {player}.
Hrmm. You may have a discount.
Hmm. Fine. You're alright too, {player}.
strings.discord.personality.villager.insult:
HRMM! Prices just went up for you, {player}.
Hmm. Rude. I'm telling the iron golem.
Hrrm. No more trades for you, {player}.
strings.discord.personality.villager.bye:
Hrmm. Bye.
Hmm. Close the door on your way out, {player}.
Hrrm. Come back with emeralds.
strings.discord.personality.villager.fallback:
Hrmm.
Hmm?
Hrrm. I don't understand, {player}.
Hmm. Got any emeralds?

strings.web.proximity.intro: Linked players opt in by joining the proximity lobby. BedrockRelay then moves nearby players into temporary voice rooms.
strings.web.proximity.noServers: Connect a Minecraft server of your own to this Discord server to use proximity voice.

strings.web.proximity.needsPermissions: Proximity voice needs the bot to have {permissions} in this Discord server. It was added before proximity voice existed, so approve its permissions again to add them.
strings.web.proximity.createHelp: BedrockRelay creates a dedicated category and a silent lobby, and manages them for you.
strings.web.proximity.createdText: The category and lobby were created and proximity voice is enabled for {server}.
strings.web.proximity.removeText: This deletes the proximity voice category, its lobby and every room in this Discord server. Anyone in them is disconnected. You can create them again later.

strings.web.language.title: Language in Discord
strings.web.language.intro: What BedrockRelay writes in this Discord server: joins, leaves and deaths, connection notices, and its answers to commands. Chat is never translated.

strings.web.language.help: Automatic follows the language in this Discord server's Community settings. Missing a language, or found a mistake? {link}

strings.web.channels.permissionHelp: Their permission settings stop BedrockRelay from seeing them or posting in them. Give the BedrockRelay role View Channel and Manage Webhooks in the channel's settings, then check again.
strings.web.events.hint: Tick none for a channel that gets only the plugin posts you choose for it, like a staff channel for alerts. Moderation says who was warned, kicked, muted or banned, by whom and why: tick it only on a staff channel.

strings.web.chatFilter.title: Chat from Minecraft
strings.web.chatFilter.label: Keep messages starting with ! in the game
strings.web.chatFilter.text: Other addons often use {prefix} for their commands, like {example}. With this on, those messages aren't sent to Discord. Chat another addon hides, like a chat ranks addon showing it again in its own format, still goes to Discord.
strings.web.autoUpdate.title: Keep the pack up to date
strings.web.autoUpdate.label: Keep the BedrockRelay pack up to date
strings.web.autoUpdate.text: When the pack goes missing from your world (after uploading a world or changing add-ons from Minecraft), or a new version is out, BedrockRelay puts it in for you with your Microsoft sign-in. It waits until nobody has been on for 10 minutes, because your Realm closes for about a minute, and does it at most once every 6 hours.
strings.web.autoUpdate.needsSignIn: This can't happen until you sign in to Microsoft again. Choose Add the pack again above to sign in.
strings.web.autoUpdate.notifyLabel: Post in a channel when it does
strings.web.autoUpdate.notifyText: A short note, so your players know why the Realm was closed for a minute.
strings.web.autoUpdate.notifyNoChannels: Connect a channel to this world first.
strings.web.autoUpdate.lastRestored: Last: the pack was added back {when}.
strings.web.autoUpdate.lastUpdated: Last: the pack was updated to v{version} {when}.
strings.web.autoUpdate.lastFailed: Last: it tried {when} and it didn't work, so it waits for you to add the pack yourself.
strings.web.ownerBot.title: Which account is the bot
strings.web.ownerBot.label: Use my Realm owner account as the bot
strings.web.ownerBot.text: Our bot takes one of your Realm's player slots. Switch this on and {account}, the account that owns this Realm, sits in the Realm as the bot instead, so every slot is free for players. Useful if you play on a different account.
strings.web.ownerBot.warning: Only for an account nobody plays on. While it's the bot, {account} is hidden in spectator mode in the End and shows as online in Minecraft all the time, and it can't join this Realm itself. When you switch this off, the next time {account} joins, its player goes back to where it was, in the game mode it had.
strings.web.ownerBot.needsSignIn: Sign in to Microsoft with the account that owns this Realm first. Choose Add the pack again above to sign in.
strings.web.ownerBot.needsPack: Update the BedrockRelay pack on this Realm to v{version} or later first.
strings.web.ownerBot.switchedOn: Your owner account joins as the bot in a moment.
strings.web.ownerBot.switchedOff: Our bot joins in a moment.
strings.web.sleep.title: When nobody's playing
strings.web.sleep.label: Leave when nobody's playing
strings.web.sleep.text: Realms host each play session in the data centre closest to whoever joins first. Our bot joins from Europe, and while it stays in, your Realm stays wherever its session started. Switch this on and the bot leaves once nobody else is in the Realm, then joins again within about a minute of someone starting to play, so your Realm is hosted near your players.
strings.web.sleep.tradeoff: While nobody's playing, nothing is relayed and messages from Discord can't reach the Realm. Chat from the first minute of a session, before the bot is back, isn't relayed, but the players who started it are still announced.
strings.web.sleep.pauses: Your Realm isn't running then either, so plugins and add-ons that work on a timer pause, and live boards keep their last update until someone plays. Leave this off if you need your Realm running all the time.
strings.web.sleep.firstToJoin: Your Realm's region setting is "Automatic, first to join", so this helps if your players live far apart.
strings.web.sleep.otherRegion: Your Realm's region setting isn't "first to join", so our bot doesn't change where it's hosted: you can leave this off.
strings.web.sleep.notMember: Our bot can't see who's playing in this Realm, so it stays in for now.
strings.web.sleep.switchedOn: Our bot leaves once nobody's playing.
strings.web.sleep.switchedOff: Our bot stays in the Realm again.
strings.web.linkedNames.title: Linked players in Discord
strings.web.linkedNames.label: Show linked players by their Discord name
strings.web.linkedNames.text: When a player has linked their Discord account with {command}, their Minecraft chat appears in Discord under their nickname and picture there. Joins, leaves and deaths still use their Minecraft name.
strings.web.relaying.title: Relaying
strings.web.relaying.label: Relay this world
strings.web.relaying.text: Switch this off to stop everything passing between {world} and Discord at once: chat both ways, joins, deaths and status notices, commands, plugin posts, live boards and proximity voice. Your channels and settings are kept, so switching it back on carries on where it left off.
strings.web.relaying.textRealm: Switch this off to stop everything passing between {world} and Discord at once: chat both ways, joins, deaths and status notices, commands, plugin posts, live boards and proximity voice. Our bot leaves the Realm while it's off and joins again when you switch it back on. Your channels and settings are kept.
strings.web.relaying.offSince: Switched off {when}. Nothing passes between this world and Discord until you switch it back on.
strings.web.relaying.offSinceRealm: Switched off {when}. Our bot has left the Realm and stays out until you switch it back on.
strings.web.relaying.realmAway: Relaying is switched off, so our bot has left the Realm

strings.web.verify.title: Verification
strings.web.verify.introServer: Members press Verify in Discord and sign in with Microsoft, so you know which Xbox account each of them is. An admin can approve each one before they're added to the allowlist of {world}.
strings.web.verify.introRealm: Members press Verify in Discord and sign in with Microsoft, so you know which Xbox account each of them is. An admin can approve each one before they're invited to {world}.
strings.web.verify.unavailable: Verification isn't available for this world right now.
strings.web.verify.noGuilds: Connect {world} to a channel first: the welcome message and the review cards go in that Discord server.
strings.web.verify.packOld: Approving adds players to the allowlist from pack {version}. Update the pack on the Settings tab. Until then, approvals wait and are applied once it's updated.
strings.web.verify.realmSignIn: To invite approved players to the Realm, BedrockRelay needs your Microsoft sign-in. Sign in again on your Account page.
strings.web.verify.enabledText: When this is off, the welcome message is removed and nobody can start a request.
strings.web.verify.savedOn: The welcome message with the Verify button is in #{channel}.
strings.web.verify.savedOff: Verification is off, and its welcome message has been removed.
strings.web.verify.posted.channel: Saved, but the welcome channel no longer exists. Pick another one.
strings.web.verify.posted.permissions: Saved, but BedrockRelay can't post in #{channel}. It needs View Channel, Send Messages and Embed Links there.
strings.web.verify.noneIn.all: No requests yet. They appear here when members press Verify.
strings.web.verify.invitedNote: Invited. They join by accepting it in Minecraft, or by pressing Verify again.
strings.web.verify.revokeTextServer: {member} loses the link and any role BedrockRelay gave them. If BedrockRelay added {gamertag} to the allowlist, they're taken off it (and kicked if they're playing). Anyone who was on the allowlist before stays on it.
strings.web.verify.revokeTextRealm: {member} loses the link and any role BedrockRelay gave them. If BedrockRelay invited {gamertag} to the Realm, they're removed from it (and kicked if they're playing). Anyone who was a member before stays a member.
strings.web.verify.problem.offline: Waiting: the server is offline. They'll be added when it's back.
strings.web.verify.problem.noAnswer: Waiting: the server didn't answer. It's tried again when the server next connects.
strings.web.verify.problem.oldPack: Waiting for pack {version}. They'll be added once the pack is updated.
strings.web.verify.problem.failed: The server couldn't add them to its allowlist.
strings.web.verify.problem.realmSignIn: Waiting: sign in to Microsoft again on your Account page.
strings.web.verify.problem.realm_signIn: Waiting: sign in to Microsoft again on your Account page.
strings.web.verify.problem.realm_blocked: They're banned from this Realm, so they weren't invited.
strings.web.verify.problem.realm_full: The Realm can't take more members.
strings.web.verify.problem.realm_expired: The Realm's subscription has run out.
strings.web.verify.setupText: Pick where the Verify button goes and where requests are reviewed. Saving posts the welcome message.
strings.web.verify.mode.approvalTextServer: Requests go to a review channel. Approving adds the player to the allowlist, links their accounts and gives them your role.
strings.web.verify.mode.approvalTextRealm: Requests go to a review channel. Approving invites the player to the Realm, links their accounts and gives them your role.
strings.web.verify.mode.linkText: Members link their Xbox account straight away, with no review, and get your role. Nobody is added to the world.
strings.web.verify.welcomeHint: Where the Verify button goes. Everyone who should be able to verify must be able to see it.
strings.web.verify.welcomeTextHint: Leave it empty to use ours. Up to {max} characters.
strings.web.verify.welcomePlaceholder: This server asks you to link your Xbox account before you play. Press the button below to get started.
strings.web.verify.welcomePlaceholderLink: Link your Xbox account to your Discord account for {world}. Press the button below to get started.
strings.web.verify.reviewHint: Requests appear here with Approve and Deny. Anyone who can see this channel can decide, so keep it private.
strings.web.verify.roleHint: Given when someone is approved, or links without review. What it unlocks is up to you.
strings.web.verify.reaskHint: How long someone waits before they can press Verify again.
strings.web.verify.enforceText: Each time the server starts, BedrockRelay switches its allowlist on, so only players on it can join. Nobody already on the allowlist is removed.
strings.web.verify.cantPost: BedrockRelay can't post in #{channel}. It needs View Channel, Send Messages and Embed Links there.
strings.web.verify.everyoneSees: Everyone in {guild} can see #{channel}, so anyone could approve themselves. Pick a private channel.
strings.web.verify.sameChannel: Use a different channel for reviews: the welcome channel is for everyone.
strings.web.verify.cantGiveRole: BedrockRelay can't give {role}. It needs Manage Roles, and its own role must be above {role} in the role list.
strings.web.verify.pickBoth: Choose a welcome channel and a review channel.
strings.web.verify.offText: Removes the welcome message and these settings. Requests and approvals are kept, and nobody loses their place in the world.
strings.web.verify.offConfirm: Turn off verification for {world}? The welcome message is removed from Discord.
strings.web.personality.title: Personality
strings.web.personality.intro: Give the bot a personality on {world}. Mention it in a connected Discord channel, or say its name in game chat, and it answers in both places.
strings.web.personality.enabledText: While this is off, the bot never replies, in Discord or in game. Your settings are kept.
strings.web.personality.relayOff: Relaying is off for this world, so the bot won't answer until it's back on.
strings.web.personality.nameHint: Players say this in game chat to talk to it, and its replies show under this name in Discord.
strings.web.personality.nicknamesHint: Up to {count} more names it answers to in game, separated by commas.
strings.web.personality.presetText.friendly: Cheerful and helpful. “Hey Steve! Good to see you.”
strings.web.personality.presetText.sarcastic: Dry and a little rude, all in fun. “Oh look, Steve's here. Alert the press.”
strings.web.personality.presetText.villager: Hrmm. Wants emeralds. “Hmm! A visitor. Do you have emeralds?”
strings.web.personality.understands: It knows greetings, goodbyes, thanks, who's online, jokes, and what it is. Anything else gets a reply in character.
strings.web.personality.inDiscord: When someone mentions the bot in Discord
strings.web.personality.inDiscordText: Anyone who @mentions the bot in a channel connected to {world}.
strings.web.personality.inGame: When a player says its name in game
strings.web.personality.inGameText: Its name or a nickname, as a word of its own in chat.
strings.web.personality.perHourHint: And one reply every few seconds for each person, so nobody can make it spam the chat.
strings.web.personality.repliesText: When a message to the bot has these words in it, it says your reply instead. Use {player} for who asked and {world} for this world's name.
strings.web.personality.replyPlaceholder: Read the rules in the welcome channel, {player}!
strings.web.personality.repliesFull: That's the most it can have: {count}.
strings.web.personality.tryText: Type what someone might say to the bot. Nothing is sent anywhere, and it uses the settings above, saved or not.

strings.web.inviteLink.introServer: One short link for joining {world}, its Discord server, or both. Share it anywhere: the page shows your server's address and a button to join Discord.

strings.web.inviteLink.showDiscordText: Players sign in with Discord and are added to the Discord server you choose.

strings.web.mc.packOutdated: {server} runs pack v{version}. v{latest} is available.
strings.web.mc.packHow: Updating installs the new pack the same way setup did: over SFTP with a preview first, or as a download. Stop the Minecraft server before you install.
strings.web.mc.packHowRealm: Updating closes the Realm until the new pack is in its world, then opens it again.
strings.web.mc.realmPackMissing: The BedrockRelay pack isn't in this world any more
strings.web.mc.realmPackMissingText: Our bot is in your Realm, but the world no longer has the BedrockRelay pack, so Discord only hears the basics. This happens when a world is uploaded or replaced, or its add-ons are changed, from Minecraft: the Realm then gets the packs on that device instead. Add the pack again, and again after any such change.
strings.web.mc.realmPluginsRetry: Try again on the Plugins tab
strings.web.mc.removeText: It stops relaying and leaves your dashboard. You can also uninstall the pack from the server. You can undo this for 7 days.
strings.web.mc.removeTextRealm: Our bot leaves the Realm and it stops relaying. You can undo this for 7 days.
strings.web.mc.removedUndo: You can undo this for 7 days under Recently removed.

strings.web.removed.title: Recently removed
strings.web.removed.introWorld: These worlds are disconnected. Undo brings back their channels and statistics exactly as they were.
strings.web.removed.intro: These Minecraft servers are disconnected. Undo brings back their channels, statistics and pack connection exactly as they were.
strings.web.removed.backText: Its channels and statistics are exactly as they were. Its pack reconnects on its next check-in.
strings.web.removed.deleteText: Its statistics and the bot's webhooks in its channels are deleted now, and it can't be undone.
strings.web.removed.deletedText: Its statistics and webhooks are gone.
strings.web.connections.title: Discord channels
strings.web.connections.none: This Minecraft server is not connected to any channel yet.
strings.web.console.title: Console
strings.web.console.intro: Run any command on {server}, as you would at its console. Only you, as its owner, can use this, and every command run here is recorded.
strings.web.console.introRealm: Run any command on {server}, as an operator could in chat, even with cheats off. Only you, as its owner, can use this, and every command run here is recorded.
strings.web.console.limitOutput: You'll see whether a command worked, not what it printed. Check in the game for the result.
strings.web.console.limitWhere: Commands run as the world itself, not as a player, so {self} matches nobody and {here} is 0, 0, 0 in the Overworld. Name players and give coordinates instead.
strings.web.console.limitConsoleOnly: Commands only the server's own console accepts, such as stop, allowlist and permission, can't be run from here.
strings.web.console.offline: This world isn't connected right now. Commands can be run once it is.
strings.web.console.relayOff: Relaying is switched off for this Realm, so our bot has left it and can't run anything there. Switch relaying back on first.
strings.web.console.asleep: Our bot left this Realm because nobody's playing. It goes back in when someone joins, and commands can be run then.
strings.web.console.botAway: Our bot isn't in this Realm right now, so commands can't reach it. They can be run once it's back in.
strings.web.commands.title: Commands from Discord
strings.web.commands.intro: People can run Minecraft commands with /relay run in a connected channel, but only the commands you allow here. Discord administrators can run any allowed command; a role widens that to its members.
strings.web.commands.connectFirst: Connect this Minecraft server to a channel first — commands are run from connected channels.
strings.web.commands.roleGone: A role that no longer exists
strings.web.commands.none: No commands are allowed yet, so /relay run refuses everything.
strings.web.commands.starWarning: * allows every command, including op, deop and stop. Only use it with a role you trust completely.
strings.web.commands.enterText: Type the command you want to allow, like weather.
strings.web.serverPlugins.intro: Plugins add Discord commands for your Minecraft world. Installed plugins appear here after the Minecraft server restarts, already switched on, so their commands are added to the Discord servers this Minecraft server is connected to. Switch one off to take its commands away. Answers are only shown to the person who asked, unless the plugin says they're for everyone. Plugins that post by themselves only post in the channels you choose.
strings.web.serverPlugins.introRealm: Plugins add Discord commands for your Minecraft world. On a Realm they go in with the BedrockRelay pack and appear here once it has reopened, already switched on, so their commands are added to the Discord servers this Realm is connected to. Switch one off to take its commands away. Answers are only shown to the person who asked, unless the plugin says they're for everyone. Plugins that post by themselves only post in the channels you choose.
strings.web.serverPlugins.connectForRoles: Connect a channel to add roles.
strings.web.serverPlugins.kindsNeedPack: Until the pack is updated to v{version}, it posts all of these.
strings.web.serverPlugins.needPack: Plugins need pack v{version} or newer
strings.web.serverPlugins.hasPack: {server} has v{version}. Update the pack, restart the Minecraft server, and its plugins will appear here.
strings.web.serverPlugins.updatesText: Updates install over SFTP like the plugins did, then take effect when the Minecraft server restarts. Your switches, roles and channels stay as they are.
strings.web.serverPlugins.updatesTextRealm: Updates go into the Realm with the BedrockRelay pack, like the plugins did: the Realm is closed until that's finished, then opens again by itself. Your switches, roles and channels stay as they are.
strings.web.serverPlugins.none: No plugins are installed on this Minecraft server yet.
strings.web.serverPlugins.noneRealm: No plugins are installed on this Realm yet.
strings.web.serverPlugins.availableIntro: Every plugin here has been reviewed, and its code is {github}. Add the ones you want to your list, then apply them in one go, over one SFTP connection. The Minecraft server loads them when it restarts. Building your own? {guide}.
strings.web.serverPlugins.availableIntroRealm: These plugins work on Realms, and every one has been reviewed; their code is {github}. Add the ones you want to your list, then apply them in one go: they go into the Realm with the BedrockRelay pack, and the Realm is closed until that's finished. Building your own? {guide}.

web.serverPlugins.serverOnly.one: {count} more plugin runs on dedicated servers only.
web.serverPlugins.serverOnly.other: {count} more plugins run on dedicated servers only.

strings.web.serverPlugins.allInstalled: Every plugin in the catalog is already on this world.
strings.web.serverPlugins.hasRealmPackHere: {server} has Realm pack v{version}. Update it on the Settings tab, then add plugins here.

strings.web.players.title: Players
strings.web.players.whileRunning: Players online show here while the server is connected.
strings.web.moderation.title: Moderation log
strings.web.moderation.messageMissing: Write the warning: it's what the player sees.
strings.web.moderation.about.warn: They see your warning in the game straight away. Nothing else happens.
strings.web.moderation.about.kick: They're disconnected straight away and see the reason on their screen. They can join again whenever they like.
strings.web.moderation.about.mute: Their chat is held back: nobody in the game sees it, and it doesn't reach Discord. They're told they're muted.
strings.web.moderation.about.muteRealm: Their chat stops reaching Discord. A Realm can't hold chat back, so other players in the Realm still see it.
strings.web.moderation.about.ban: They can't join until the ban ends or you lift it, even with a new gamertag. If they're online, they're kicked now.
strings.web.moderation.about.banRealm: They go on the Realm's own ban list, which also takes away their membership. If they're online, they're kicked now.
strings.web.moderation.about.removeServer: They're taken off the server's allowlist, and kicked if they're online. That keeps them out only while the allowlist is on.
strings.web.moderation.about.removeRealm: They're taken off the Realm's members, and kicked if they're online. They can't come back without a new invite.
strings.web.moderation.needsSignIn: Needs the Realm owner's Microsoft sign-in: sign in again from the Settings tab
strings.web.moderation.needsAllowlistPack: Needs BedrockRelay pack 0.7.0 or newer: update it from the Settings tab
strings.web.moderation.note.kickFailed: The world didn't kick them, but they'll be refused the next time they join.
strings.web.moderation.note.packOld: This server's pack is out of date, so they're kicked as they join instead of being refused, and muted chat only stays out of Discord.
strings.web.moderation.note.realmNotListed: The Realm's own ban list couldn't be used, so they're kicked whenever they join while our bot is in the Realm.
strings.web.moderation.note.realmChatOnly: Other players in the Realm still see their chat.
strings.web.moderation.note.realmRejoin: Banning took away their Realm membership, so they'll need inviting again.
strings.web.moderation.sanctionsNone: Nobody is banned or muted here.
strings.web.moderation.packOld: This server's BedrockRelay pack is older than {version}: banned players are kicked as they join instead of being refused, and muted chat only stays out of Discord. Update the pack from the Settings tab.
strings.web.moderation.realmNoList: The Realm owner's Microsoft sign-in isn't working, so bans can't go on the Realm's own ban list: banned players are kicked whenever they join while our bot is in. Sign in again from the Settings tab.
strings.web.moderation.moderatorsIntro: Members with these roles can use {command} on this world to warn, kick, mute and ban players. You always can.
strings.web.moderation.moderatorsNone: Connect a Discord channel to this world first: the roles come from its Discord server.
strings.web.players.detailsNeedPack: Player details (inventory, health, where they are) need BedrockRelay pack {version} or newer. Update the pack to see them.
strings.web.players.detailsNeedRealmPack: Player details (inventory, health, where they are) need the Realm pack {version} or newer.
strings.web.inspect.asOfViewed: As of {when}, the last time they were viewed
strings.web.inspect.noAnswer: {server} didn't answer in time, so this is what was saved before.
strings.web.inspect.gone: They've just left, so this is what was saved before.
strings.web.inspect.packTooOld: Live details need BedrockRelay pack {version} or newer on this server. Update the pack from this page.
strings.web.inspect.packTooOldRealm: Live details need the Realm pack {version} or newer.
strings.web.inspect.nothingSaved: Nothing has been saved about them yet.
strings.web.inspect.slot.head: Helmet
strings.web.inspect.pick: Select an item to see its enchantments, durability and contents.
strings.web.security.title: Security
strings.web.security.intro: Your pack proves who it is with a token that's built in when it's installed. If the pack zip or its config files may have leaked, revoke every token; reinstalling issues a new one.
strings.web.security.warning: The pack on {server} stops connecting straight away and stays quiet until you reinstall it. Use this if your pack zip or config files may have been seen by someone else.
strings.web.security.revokedText: The pack on {server} can't connect until you reinstall it, which issues a new token.
strings.web.join.title: Where players join
strings.web.join.label: Join address
strings.web.join.whileRunning: Checked while the Minecraft server is running.
strings.web.join.okAnswers: Players can join at {address} — it answers as “{name}”.
strings.web.join.blankText: It answers at {address}, but with no server details, so Minecraft treats it as offline. Turn on {setting} in server.properties or your host's panel, then restart.
strings.web.join.silentText: Nothing answered at {address}. Check the port is open to players, or if players use a different address, enter it below.
strings.web.join.unresolvedText: {address} doesn't resolve to a server. Check it for typos.
strings.web.join.private: It connects from a private address ({address}), so we can't check it from the internet. If players join from outside your network, enter the address they use below.
strings.web.join.automaticText: {server} is checked at the address it connects from again.
strings.web.join.hintSet: BedrockRelay checks this address about once a minute while the server is running.
strings.web.join.hintAutomatic: Leave empty to check the address your Minecraft server connects from, on the port in server.properties. Enter the address players use if that's different, e.g. play.example.com:19132.
strings.web.realm.connecting: The bot is joining the Realm.
strings.web.realm.down: The bot can't get into the Realm: {error}
strings.web.realm.downNoReason: The bot can't get into the Realm right now. It keeps trying.
strings.web.realm.paused: Paused: the bot stays out of the Realm until it's resumed.
strings.web.realm.asleep: Nobody's playing. Our bot joins as soon as someone does.
strings.web.realm.banned: Banned from the Realm: the bot has stopped trying to join.
strings.web.realm.bannedText: The Realm banned {bot}, our bot, so it has stopped trying to join and nothing is relayed to Discord. If it was a mistake, or an add-on such as an anti-cheat did it, unban {bot} in Minecraft, then choose Try again.
strings.web.realm.removeText: The bot leaves the Realm and its channels stop. You can undo this for 7 days.
strings.web.uninstall.title: Remove {server}?
strings.web.uninstall.intro: It is disconnected from every Discord channel straight away, and its pack is no longer accepted. You can undo this from your dashboard for 7 days; after that it is gone for good.
strings.web.uninstall.justRemoveText: The pack stays on your Minecraft server but can no longer connect. You can uninstall it yourself whenever you like.
strings.web.uninstall.alsoUninstall: Also uninstall the pack over SFTP
strings.web.uninstall.alsoUninstallText: We connect once, show exactly what will change, and remove only what BedrockRelay added.
strings.web.uninstall.nothingText: No BedrockRelay files were found in that folder. Removing will only disconnect it from BedrockRelay.
strings.web.uninstall.betaText: Turn it off only if nothing else on the world needs it. Achievements stay disabled for the world either way — Bedrock never re-enables them once an experiment has been used.
strings.web.uninstall.manualWorld: In {file}, delete the entry whose pack_id is {id}. Keep every other entry.
strings.web.uninstall.manualConfig: In {variables} delete the keys starting with {prefix}, and in {secrets} delete {token}. If there is a {folder} folder, delete it.
strings.web.uninstall.manualBeta: Optionally turn Beta APIs off in your world settings, if no other pack needs it. Achievements stay disabled for that world either way.
strings.web.setup.subtitle: From Discord invite to pack installation, all in one place.
strings.web.setup.step1: Add the bot to a Discord server
strings.web.setup.realmUpdateText: We put the new pack into your Realm's world, the same way as when you set it up. Your channels and settings stay as they are.
strings.web.setup.updateText: Install the new pack over the old one, then restart your Minecraft server. Your channels and settings stay as they are.
strings.web.setup.newTitle: Let's get your Minecraft server talking to Discord.
strings.web.setup.newText: Five short steps, one at a time. Everything happens here in your dashboard.
strings.web.setup.guildNeededText: Create a Discord server, or ask for Manage Server permission in one, before setting up BedrockRelay.
strings.web.setup.inviteWaiting: Discord says BedrockRelay was added. Waiting for it to arrive in {guild}…
strings.web.setup.inviteCancelled: The bot was not added. You can try again whenever you're ready.
strings.web.setup.inviteNeeded: BedrockRelay needs to join {guild}. You'll approve it on Discord and come straight back here.
strings.web.setup.nameNeededText: Give your Minecraft server a name, like the one players know it by.
strings.web.setup.nameText: How it's labelled in Discord and on your dashboard.
strings.web.setup.addressText: Enter the address players use to join. We'll ping it to find its name and check that players can reach it.
strings.web.setup.addressHint: Like play.example.com or 203.0.113.5:19135. Leave the port off if it's 19132.
strings.web.setup.addressNeededText: Enter the address players type to join your Minecraft server.
strings.web.setup.noAnswer.silent: Nothing answered on that port. The server may be stopped, the port may be different, or a firewall may be blocking it.
strings.web.setup.noAnswer.blank: The server answered but hid its details, so players' server lists show it as offline. Set enable-lan-visibility=true in server.properties.
strings.web.setup.noAnswer.private: That's an address on a private network, so players outside it can't reach it, and neither can we.
strings.web.setup.noAnswer.unresolved: We couldn't find that address. Check the spelling.
strings.web.setup.noAnswerContinue: You can still set it up now and fix the address later from its page.
strings.web.setup.matchTitle: That's {server}, which you've already set up
strings.web.setup.matchText: Use it with this Discord server too, rather than setting it up a second time.
strings.web.setup.matchHereText: It already relays to this Discord server, so there's nothing more to set up.
strings.web.setup.matchStartedText: It's on this Discord server but has no channel yet. Carry on where you left off.
strings.web.setup.different: It's a different server. Set it up as a new one.
strings.web.setup.notRunning: Server not running right now? Name it yourself instead.
strings.web.setup.advancedHint: Leave these alone unless your host tells you otherwise.
strings.web.setup.moduleConfig: Use a per-module config folder instead of config/default (VPS or self-hosted Minecraft servers only)
strings.web.setup.stopFirst: Stop your Minecraft server first, then choose how to install.
strings.web.setup.waitingVersion: Waiting for {server} to connect with pack v{version}…
strings.web.setup.waitingText: Start (or restart) your Minecraft server. This page moves on by itself the moment the pack checks in.
strings.web.setup.trouble1: Beta APIs must be on for the world. Without it the pack loads but stays silent.
strings.web.setup.trouble2: Your console should show a line starting [BedrockRelay] connected to. No [BedrockRelay] line at all means the pack did not load.
strings.web.setup.trouble3: Make sure the server is running the world the pack was installed to.
strings.web.setup.skipChoose: Skip for now and choose a channel
strings.web.setup.notConnectedYet: Not connected yet. It starts relaying as soon as it does.
strings.web.setup.runningPack: {server} is running pack v{version}. Its channels and settings are just as they were.
strings.web.setup.nextStart: The new pack takes over the next time {server} starts. Its channels and settings are just as they were.
strings.web.setup.relayingTo: {server} is relaying to {channels}. Say something in Minecraft to see it arrive.
strings.web.setup.channelText: Minecraft chat, joins, leaves and deaths will appear in this channel, and messages sent there will appear in Minecraft. You can add more channels and filters afterwards.
strings.web.setup.noChannels: This Discord server has no text channels yet. Create one, then refresh.
strings.web.install.addedTo: BedrockRelay will be added to {world}, alongside any packs already there.
strings.web.install.backedUp: Every existing file we change is backed up first, next to the original.
strings.web.install.betaOn: Beta APIs will be turned on. Achievements are disabled for this world from now on.
strings.web.install.betaTitle: Beta APIs must be on for this world
strings.web.install.betaText: BedrockRelay reads chat through a Minecraft feature that is still experimental, so it cannot work without Beta APIs. Turning on any experiment permanently disables achievements for this world.
strings.web.install.betaAccept: Turn on Beta APIs for this world. I understand achievements will be disabled for it permanently.
strings.web.install.connecting: Connecting to your Minecraft server and preparing a preview…
strings.web.install.notBds: This folder does not look like a Bedrock server.
strings.web.install.noWorlds: No worlds were found. Start your Minecraft server once to create one.
strings.web.install.sftpIntro: Your SFTP details are in your host's control panel. We show every planned change before writing anything. Your password or key is used for this one connection and never stored; the host, port, username and folder are kept with your world, so next time you only type the password.
strings.web.download.doneText: Follow the installation steps below it to put it on your Minecraft server.
strings.web.download.intro: Download a pack with your Minecraft server's settings already filled in. Keep the zip private because it contains your installation token.
strings.web.download.step2: Unzip into the folder with server.properties and worlds/. Merge files rather than replacing other packs.
strings.web.download.step3: Add the BedrockRelay entry from INSTALL.txt to the top of your world's world_behavior_packs.json, keeping existing entries below it.
strings.web.download.step4: Turn on Beta APIs for the world. It is required, and like any experiment it permanently disables achievements for that world.
strings.web.catalog.empty: There are no plugins in the catalog yet.
strings.web.catalog.notForRealmsAdmin: Not marked for Realms (as admin you can try it)
strings.web.catalog.realmPackMissing: The Realm pack isn't in this Realm yet
strings.web.catalog.realmNotRunning: Chosen, but not running: add it again or remove it
strings.web.catalog.realmClosesTitle: {realm} is closed until this is finished
strings.web.catalog.realmClosesText: We download its world, add the pack with these plugins and upload it again. Anyone playing is disconnected, and the Realm opens again by itself when it's done.
strings.web.catalog.untestedTextHere: Not checked on a Realm yet, which runs without Beta APIs. A plugin that needs them won't load, and the Plugins tab will say so.
strings.web.catalog.realmSignIn: Sign in to Microsoft again on the Realm's setup first.
strings.web.catalog.showDetails: Show details and install options for {plugin}
strings.web.catalog.restartLoad: Restart {server} to load them. Each one is switched on as soon as it's loaded.
strings.web.catalog.manualSummary: Download it and install it yourself

web.catalog.manualFolder.one: Put it in {folder} on your Minecraft server.
web.catalog.manualFolder.other: Put them in {folder} on your Minecraft server.

strings.web.catalog.manualIndex: In {file}, add {names} to the list, e.g. {example}.
strings.web.catalog.manualRestart: Restart the Minecraft server, then switch each plugin on from its page.
strings.web.catalog.restartText: Plugins load when a Minecraft server starts, so these changes take effect the next time you restart {server}. It can keep running while we copy the files.
strings.web.catalog.touchOnly: We touch only these plugins' files and their lines in the plugin list, exactly as reviewed, over one connection. Your SFTP details are used once and never stored.
strings.web.catalog.touchOnlyOwn: We touch only these plugins' files and their lines in the plugin list, over one connection. Your own plugins are installed exactly as you uploaded them. Your SFTP details are used once and never stored.
strings.web.catalog.own.onlyYou: Your own plugin · only you can see it
strings.web.catalog.own.title: Your own plugins
strings.web.catalog.own.intro: Upload a plugin you've written for your own Minecraft worlds. It isn't reviewed, and it's listed only here, on your dashboard. It installs like any other plugin.
strings.web.catalog.own.uploadHelp: Choose the plugin's .js file. We read its {id}, name, {version} and description, and check its format. Uploading a file with the same id again replaces it. {guide}.
strings.web.catalog.own.newVersionHelp: Choose the updated .js file, with a higher {version}, so your Minecraft worlds are offered the update. {guide}.
strings.web.catalog.own.notReviewedText: It runs in your Minecraft world with the Minecraft Script API, so only upload code you wrote or trust. The BedrockRelay team can see what's uploaded and where it's used.
strings.web.catalog.own.addedHere: It's under Your own plugins, ready to install.
strings.web.catalog.own.updatedText: Version {version} is ready. Add the update to your list to install it.
strings.web.catalog.own.differentId: That file's id is {id}, not {was}, so it was added as a separate plugin.
strings.web.catalog.own.deleteText: It's removed from your dashboard. You can upload it again at any time.
strings.web.catalog.own.blockedShort: Blocked by BedrockRelay: you can only remove it.
strings.web.catalog.own.blocked: BedrockRelay has blocked this plugin. It's switched off on all your Minecraft worlds and can't be installed or updated. Remove it from your worlds, then delete it.
strings.web.catalog.own.blockedWhy: BedrockRelay has blocked this plugin: {reason} It's switched off on all your Minecraft worlds and can't be installed or updated. Remove it from your worlds, then delete it.
strings.web.setup.worldTitle: Let's get your world talking to Discord.
strings.web.setup.worldText: A few short steps, one at a time. Everything happens here in your dashboard.
strings.web.setup.kindText: BedrockRelay works with both. The steps after this one depend on which you choose.
strings.web.setup.kindRealmText: The world you pay Mojang to host, joined from the Realms tab in Minecraft.
strings.web.setup.kindRealmPoint1: Sign in with the Realm owner's Microsoft account
strings.web.setup.kindRealmPoint2: Our bot joins your Realm, hidden from players
strings.web.setup.kindRealmPoint3: No files or server access needed
strings.web.setup.kindBdsText: A server you run yourself or rent from a host, joined by address and port.
strings.web.setup.kindBdsPoint1: Installs our behavior pack on your server
strings.web.setup.kindBdsPoint2: Over SFTP from here, or as a download
strings.web.setup.realmStepSignIn: Sign in as the Realm owner
strings.web.setup.realmSignInText: Sign in with the Microsoft account that owns the Realm. We use it to:
strings.web.setup.realmSignInWhy1: List your Realms, so you can pick the right one

strings.web.setup.realmPackText: The BedrockRelay pack goes into your Realm's world. With it, our bot:

strings.web.setup.realmPackDoes2: Can run commands from Discord, even with cheats off
strings.web.setup.realmPackDoes3: Shares player positions for proximity voice
strings.web.setup.realmPackHow: We close your Realm, download its world, add the pack, upload it and open the Realm again. Other packs aren't touched. It takes a few minutes, longer for a big world, and anyone playing is disconnected meanwhile.

strings.web.setup.realmManualText: Add the pack to your Realm yourself in Minecraft. Your Realm isn't closed or re-uploaded, which suits big worlds. The file already carries your Realm's own secret.
strings.web.setup.realmManualStep1: Open the downloaded .mcpack file on a device with Minecraft. Minecraft imports the BedrockRelay pack.
strings.web.setup.realmManualStep2: In Minecraft, go to Play, then the Realms tab, and open your Realm's hub. Choose World, then Edit World, and under Behavior Packs activate BedrockRelay.
strings.web.setup.realmManualStep3: Press Play, then Save Changes. Minecraft uploads the pack and reloads your Realm, and this step finishes by itself once the pack answers our bot.
strings.web.setup.realmManualWaiting: Waiting for the pack to answer our bot…
strings.web.setup.realmPackManualDone: Adding the pack yourself: our bot hides once it answers

strings.web.account.microsoftWhy: We use it only with Minecraft Realms, and only on Realms you own: to list them, invite our relay bot, and add or update the BedrockRelay pack.
strings.web.account.microsoftNever: It's kept encrypted, never used to join a Realm unless you choose it as a Realm's bot, never used to sign in anywhere else as you, and deleted the moment you sign out below.

strings.web.account.data3: If you've connected Microsoft for Realms: your gamertag and your sign-in, encrypted, until you sign out.
strings.web.account.data4: No chat archive, no email address, and nothing sold or used for advertising.
